question: On 17 July, Commissioner Zaharieva replied to my follow-up question E-001557/20261, which followed on from my original question E-000437/2026(ASW)2. In her reply, she stated, amongst other things, the following: ‘Proposals received under Horizon Europe are evaluated solely by independent experts, and proposals submitted to the CERV programmes are evaluated by the Commission assisted by independent external experts.
Only the highest ranked proposals that best align with the objectives of the programmes are selected for funding.’ In light of this reply, I have the following follow-up questions: 1.
Can the Commission explain how these ‘independent experts’ are selected, what their background is (especially their political background), and what (legal) relationship they have with the Commission?

Can the Commission explain the precise criteria used to identify ‘the highest ranked proposals’? What criteria – political, in particular – underpin this, perhaps drawing an analogy with the current European public procurement criteria?

Can the Commission state, in detail and in concrete terms, whether it considers ‘confronting the rise of populism’ to be so important that it wishes to finance this effort through an NGO such as ECPS?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (17.11.2026) 1. Independent external experts1 are selected following a corporate call for expression of interest for the period 2021-20272. Selection is based on objective criteria including expertise, experience, language skills, geographical, sectorial and gender balance, rotation, and absence of conflicts of interest. Political background is not considered.

Selected experts sign a contract3 with the Commission or its executive agencies setting out their tasks, rights and obligations. Breaches of contractual obligations may lead to rejection or reduction of remuneration, termination of the contract, and administrative sanctions such as exclusion from EU award procedures or financial penalties. 2.

Selection and award criteria, and the evaluation procedure, are published in the relevant call documents and reflect each programme’s objectives. Under the Horizon Europe Regulation4, for example, the award criteria are excellence, impact, and quality and efficiency of implementation, while under the Citizens, Equality, Rights and Values Programme5 they are relevance, quality and impact.

Proposals are evaluated according to the rules set out in the Financial Regulation6. Grants are awarded through a highly competitive process in which the highest-ranked proposals that best match the objectives of the programmes are selected for funding. The evaluation procedure is governed by equal treatment and transparency, ensuring no conflict of interest. No political criteria are involved. 3.
As indicated in the answer to written question E-000437/20267, the objectives of EU funding are defined in programmes established by basic acts adopted by the European Parliament and the Council8.
1 The Financial Regulation expressly provides that ‘external experts may assist the evaluation committee

pursuant to a decision of the authorising officer responsible’ and that ‘members of the evaluation committee may be external experts where that possibility is provided for in the basic act’ (See Article 153(3) of the Financial Regulation), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2024/2509/oj/eng.

The Horizon Europe Regulation states that ‘proposals shall be evaluated by the evaluation committee which shall be composed of independent external experts’ (See Article 29 of the Horizon Europe Regulation), https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2021/695/oj/eng. 2 https://ec.europa.eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/docs/2021-2027/experts/call-for-expression-ofinterest_en.pdf. 3 https://ec.europa.

eu/info/funding-tenders/opportunities/docs/2021-2027/experts/model-contract_en.pdf. 4 See footnote 1. 5 https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/reg/2021/692/oj. 6 See footnote 1. 7 https://www.europarl.europa.eu/doceo/document/E-10-2026-000437_EN.html. 8 The programmes are implemented through work programmes adopted by the Commission in accordance with the comitology procedure involving representatives of the Member States.
